text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An explosion wrecked the apartment of a senior Albanian appeals court judge early on Wednesday. The fourth and fifth floor of the building in central Tirana where judge Prel Martini lived suffered widespread damage.

- A safe belonging to the late communist dictator Enver Hoxha's son-in-law Klement Kolaneci, arrested for his connections with a guerrilla group, turned out to not have vast sums of money stashed away in it.
- Albanian appeals court upheld the verdict of the Tirana court on nine former senior communist officials sentenced for human rights abuses.
- The Pyramide scheme has taken Albanians back to the old days when they had to queue all night to receive their money.
- Kuwait has asked the Albanian national soccer team to hold a friendly match but Tirana has yet to answer.
- Five people were injured when rival gangster bands clashed with eachother. Police have arrested five gangsters.
- According to the World Bank, Albania's GNP is $690 per capita.
- Twenty NATO member countries and other countries will take part in a workshop in Albania from Wednesday to Friday on the incorporation of NATO doctrine into national armies.
- President Sali Berisha sends telegrams of congratulations to the Bulgarian President Peter Stoyanov and the Romanian Democratic Convention for their victory in the elections.

- Opposition parties complain the final results statement from the Central Electoral Commission on the local elections did not mention any irregularities. The parties therefore did not sign the statement.
